Thanks, this is a good fit and the right size: a small local helper emitted at each declaration, matching what the Rust generators do. Comments sit directly above their declarations, and undocumented entities produce the same output as before. A few gaps, inline:

- **Events without fields lose their docs entirely**, and handle methods (plain, `DynamicFsmHandle`, FSM transitions) never get event docs. See the inline comment.
- **`/*` in a doc fails `-Wall -Werror`** (agreeing with the existing CodeRabbit comment). There is also a carriage-return edge case in the same helper. See inline.
- Minor:
  - The entity doc goes on `XObserver` and the marker struct, but not on `Handle<X>`, which is what users hold.
  - Unicode direction-control characters in a doc fail `-Werror=bidi-chars`.
  - Whitespace-only doc lines emit trailing spaces, and `doc: ""` emits an empty `/** */` block.
- Tests: please add cases for the comment escaping, an event without fields, and FSM payloads (where the sequence field is filtered out).

If handle-method docs are left for a follow-up, please say so in the description, since #862 will need to stay open. Heads-up: drafts #889 and #740 both touch the same functions in `facade.rs`.

review_comments.body:
Events with no public fields hit this `continue` before `emit_docs`. Many events in `examples/readme/model.yaml` have no fields, including all the FSM states. The handle methods (`Handle<T>::...`, `DynamicFsmHandle`, and the typed FSM transitions from `emit_fsm_method_declaration`) don't emit event docs either, so a documented event without fields has no documentation anywhere in `quent.hpp`.

The generated Rust code documents both the payload and the handle method (`crates/instrumentation-build/src/runtime/handle/mod.rs`, `handle/fsm/mod.rs`). Emitting `event.annotations().docs()` with `"  "` indentation before each handle and transition method would close this gap. The methods are also what users see on IDE hover.

Only `*/` is escaped. A `/*` inside the block comment, e.g. a doc that says `logs/*.json`, triggers `-Wcomment` and fails `-Wall -Werror`. I reproduced this with g++. The current replacement can also create one: `/*/` becomes `/* /`. Please escape both delimiters and add a test case containing both.

`str::lines()` only splits on `
`, so an interior `` stays in the line. C++ treats `` as a line ending, so backslash line-splicing can form `*/` after escaping. For example, `doc: "*\/#error injected/*"` ends the comment early, and g++ then reports `#error injected`. This needs an explicit escape in a double-quoted YAML string, so it is an edge case. Normalizing `
` and `` to `
` before splitting would fix it. Stripping or escaping control and bidi characters at the same point would also avoid `-Wbidi-chars`.

Thanks for the review. Pushed a follow-up commit:
- Event docs are now emitted on `Handle<T>` methods, `DynamicFsmHandle` methods and FSM transition declarations, so fieldless events keep their docs. The entity doc is also on `Handle<X>`, `FsmHandle` and `DynamicFsmHandle`.
- Both `/*` and `*/` are escaped, `\r\n`/`\r` are normalized, control and bidi characters are stripped, and empty or whitespace-only docs emit nothing.
- Added tests for the escaping, fieldless events and an FSM with only the filtered `seq` field. YAML `fsms` states don't accept `doc`, so that test builds the schema through the API.

Separately: a doc containing a bare CR or bidi characters also fails to compile in the generated Rust code; this PR does not change that.
